body: Here's food for thought: _which_ whitespaces do we want to trim? Just spaces, tabs and all sorts of newlines? Or do we look into other sorts of separator characters supported by Unicode?

There used to be a good-looking document from the Guava guys linked from their [`CharMatcher.whitespace()` javadoc](http://google.github.io/guava/releases/22.0/api/docs/com/google/common/base/CharMatcher.html#whitespace--) that covered different definitions of "whitespace", [but it appears to be dead now](https://spreadsheets.google.com/pub?key=pd8dAQyHbdewRsnE5x5GzKQ).
We just mean the `trim()` method provided in `java.lang.String`: nothing more, nothing less.
Is there any particular reason that we use `String.trim()` over any other string-trimming strategy?
It's built-in, simple, and meets our needs.
Cool, that's completely fair. Thank you very much for answering my questions!

**Analysis**:

Any tags supplied to `org.junit.platform.launcher.TagFilter.includeTags(List<String>)` or `org.junit.platform.launcher.TagFilter.excludeTags(List<String>)` are already trimmed via `org.junit.platform.launcher.TagFilter.trimmedTagsOf(TestDescriptor)`. This includes user-supplied tags passed in via the console launcher, Maven Surefire provider, and the Gradle plugin.

Neither `org.junit.jupiter.engine.descriptor.JupiterTestDescriptor.getTags(AnnotatedElement)` nor `org.junit.platform.engine.TestTag.create(String)` currently performs any trimming.

**Correction:**

`TagFilter.includeTags()` and `TagFilter.excludeTags()` currently trim tags stored in a `TestDescriptor` but do **not** trim the tags used to create the filter.

issue.body:
## Overview

Although tags are currently _trimmed_ (see #942), they are otherwise allowed to contain any type of character. However, this makes it more difficult to reason about a tag expression language as proposed in #927 and can lead to subtle configuration errors.

## Related Issues

- #927 
- #942 

## Deliverables

- [x] Disallow [whitespace](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Character.html#isWhitespace-int-) and [control characters](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Character.html#isISOControl-int-) within tags, after trimming.
